findings.evidence: Page 10, §1.2 Mental Model: "for non-AR generation the same reasoning runs on model evaluations instead of output tokens, and §2.1.2 (latent video) and §3.1.1 (diffusion/LLaDA-style) carry the extension."
findings.issue: The cross-reference labels §2.1.2 as '(latent video)'. The actual section heading on page 59 is 'The work unit changes with the generator'. While the section does discuss latent video as its example, the parenthetical label does not match the section title, making it harder for a reader using the TOC or section headings to locate the referenced content. The convention elsewhere in the book (e.g., '§7.3 (mechanism inventory)') uses paraphrased topic labels that are clearly descriptive; '(latent video)' is a topic label but does not match any heading.
findings.fix_instruction: Either use the actual section title ('§2.1.2 (the work unit changes with the generator)') or a more general label ('§2.1.2 (non-text generation)') that the reader can match to the heading.

findings.evidence: Figure label on page 9: "figure 1.1: The KV cache…". Figure label on page 11: "figure 1.2: How a token travels…". Cross-reference in Fig. 1.1 caption: "The full token-travel pipeline is in Fig 1.2 and the end-to-end pipeline in Fig 2.1". Cross-reference in Fig. 1.2 caption: "the full read-side mechanics and the iterative loop are shown in Fig 2.1".
findings.issue: The figure labels use the form 'figure N.M' (lowercase word, period separator: 'figure 1.1', 'figure 1.2') but the cross-references within captions use 'Fig N.M' (abbreviated, space separator: 'Fig 1.2', 'Fig 2.1'). The Preface's cross-reference convention section defines only '§ N.M' for sections and says 'the appendix's figures carry A.N' — it does not specify a figure cross-reference form. The internal inconsistency between 'figure 1.1' (label) and 'Fig 1.2' (reference) is a recurring pattern across the document: e.g., page 17 'Fig 2.1', page 148 'Fig 6.1'. The book should pick one form.
findings.fix_instruction: Standardize all figure cross-references to one form (e.g., 'Fig. 1.2') and state the convention in the Preface reading-conventions paragraph alongside the § convention.

findings.evidence: Fig. 1.1 caption ends: "[ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] — a schematic of a documented mechanism, not a screenshot or a measurement". Preface, PDF p. 19 (printed p. xv): "ILLUSTRATIVE (Axis 1, provenance) — a non-canonical worked example ([ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED)" and "FACT — directly stated by the source." The adjacent Fig. 1.2 caption (PDF p. 35, printed p. 11) uses "[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]" for a schematic of the same kind.
findings.issue: Axis-1/Axis-2 label-pair mismatch against the book's own declared vocabulary: ILLUSTRATIVE is declared to pair with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED, and FACT ("directly stated by the source") contradicts the caption's own statement that the drawing is the author's schematic rather than a measurement. As written the tag asserts both a non-canonical provenance and a first-party factual assertion.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-label Fig. 1.1 as [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] (or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]) for the drawing, and, if a FACT claim about the underlying mechanism is intended, give it its own source-cited tag (e.g. "[1P][FACT] for the mechanism; [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] for the schematic").

findings.chapter: Preface (Evidence cutoff and edition date) vs Ch 1
findings.evidence: Preface: "Primary sources (arXiv reports, model cards, vendor pages) were accessed as of the build date and each is cited with a stable identifier in the References chapter" (build v20260913, dated 2026-09-13) and "Adding a source, or changing a value, is what requires a new build identifier or a named addendum." Ch 1 (p. 31): "post dated 2026-04-22 — inside the 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff; retrieved 2026-11-15, an access date only, since access dates are not evidence dates, so no addendum revision applies".
findings.issue: The apparatus contradicts itself: a source 'retrieved 2026-11-15' cannot have been 'accessed as of the build date' (2026-09-13), and per the book's own rule, adding a source requires a new build identifier or a named addendum — neither of which is recorded for this citation. The carve-out ('access dates are not evidence dates') addresses evidence status but not the build/attribution contradiction.
findings.fix_instruction: Either carry the vLLM FP8-KV citation under a named addendum revision (as done for the 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-01 notes), or restate the Preface rule so that a post-build access timestamp on an in-cutoff source is explicitly permitted without a new build identifier.

findings.evidence: Fig 1.1 (p. 33): "[ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] — a schematic of a documented mechanism, not a screenshot or a measurement". Preface contract (p. 21): "[ILLUSTRATIVE] is reserved for a non-canonical hypothetical worked example: its inputs are [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and its derived results [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]." Bare tags with no Axis-2 partner: "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]" (Figs 2.1 p. 44, 4.1 p. 112, 5.1 p. 134, 6.1 p. 137), "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual, roofline developed in Ch 8]" (Fig 2.2 p. 52), "[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]" (Fig 6.2 p. 140); Figs 3.1/3.2 (pp. 61–62) carry no evidence tag at all.
findings.issue: Caption evidence-tag grammar violates the book's own label contract: [ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] is a pairing the Preface's mapping does not define (ILLUSTRATIVE is restricted to ASSUMPTION/DERIVED results of worked examples, not documented-mechanism schematics); the bare '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' tags lack the mandated one-Axis-1-plus-one-Axis-2 pair; and sibling conceptual figures (3.1, 3.2) are untagged, so identical figure types are treated three different ways.
findings.fix_instruction: Define one figure-schematic convention in the Preface (e.g., permit [ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] explicitly for documented-mechanism schematics, or introduce a dedicated tag), then apply it uniformly to every conceptual figure including Figs 3.1/3.2, and require the Axis-2 partner on all caption tags.
